item.title: Trump scores Supreme Court win on mail-in voting restrictions before midterms
item.description: The Supreme Court’s order clears the Trump administration to immediately enforce revised mail-ballot restrictions in 23 states ahead of November’s midterms.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court on Monday handed the Trump administration a victory, allowing it to enforce President Donald Trump’s "election integrity" executive order restricting mail-in voting ahead of the November midterms. 

The high court lifted an injunction that had blocked the order in 23 states that challenged it after the administration appealed in July; Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented. 

The U.S. Postal Service and Justice Department said they would immediately implement the revised mail-ballot restrictions after the ruling.

The decision appears to leave room for additional court challenges that could further slow Trump’s order.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: WNBA reportedly says Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are ineligible, but won't explain why
item.description: The WNBA reportedly declared Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White ineligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft but has not defined "woman" under its CBA.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA has apparently decided Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White aren't eligible to play in the league.

Now it needs to say, on the record, how it reached that decision.

WNBA SILENT AFTER CAITLIN CLARK SAYS LEAGUES SHOULD DETERMINE WHO SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Front Office Sports reported Monday that unnamed league sources said Freedom and White, two former NBA players who have declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft, are ineligible.

The sources also called their declarations "simply publicity stunts" and said the league would not give oxygen to efforts intended to mock it or demean others.

Fine.

What makes them ineligible?

That's the only question that matters, and the WNBA still won't answer it.

Freedom and White are obviously making a point. Nobody thinks either man is seriously preparing to spend next season trying to earn a WNBA roster spot.

But calling it a stunt doesn't make the point go away.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement says only players who are women are eligible to play in the league. As the FOS report itself acknowledges, the CBA does not define "woman" or include language about "gender identity" or "sex assigned at birth."

That's a problem for the WNBA, and it's not a problem that was created by Freedom or White.

CLUELESS WNBA ATTACKS 'BAD-FAITH' FANS WHO DON'T WANT BIOLOGICAL MEN RUINING WOMEN'S SPORTS

If the league has now determined that two males who say they identify as women do not satisfy the eligibility standard, it should be able to explain the standard it used.

Does the WNBA define "woman" based on biological sex? If so, say it.

Is self-identification insufficient? If so, say that too.

Does the league use a different set of criteria for someone who identifies as transgender? If it does, players and prospective draft entrants deserve to know those criteria before the 2027 WNBA Draft.

The league has reportedly already made the call. It says neither Freedom nor White can play.

Now it needs to explain its rule.

The WNBA doesn't get to make that determination anonymously, dismiss the challenge as a publicity stunt and pretend there is nothing to discuss.

OutKick asked the WNBA to confirm whether the FOS report reflects its official position, identify the criteria used to determine Freedom and White are ineligible, define "woman" under Article XIII, Section 1(a) of the CBA and say whether the league will publish written guidance before the draft.

The WNBA didn't respond to our request before publication.

It did, however, have unnamed sources tell Front Office Sports that Freedom and White are ineligible.

Nobody can prove the WNBA chose Front Office Sports because it expected an easy story. But Salao's coverage gives the league every reason to believe it would get one.

WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED

Earlier this month, FOS described OutKick as an outlet that had "glommed onto" the issue and ran a subhead about outlets that "pop in to write about transgender issues." The reporter didn't write that as a simple credential story. He adopted the league's premise that OutKick was trying to manufacture a controversy.

FOS also used the Sky's credential decision to make OutKick look unreliable.

It reported that, "as of Friday morning," a Sky source said no decision had been made, then emphasized that OutKick had not shared a rejection email. The Sky denied the request at approximately 3:45 p.m. ET. FOS published at 5:46 p.m. and updated at 8:07 p.m. without telling readers that the denial had already happened.

Maybe that was all a coincidence. It would mean the Sky source had no idea Friday morning how the request would be resolved, nobody told FOS when it was denied and no one at FOS thought to check before it published or updated.

That's a lot to believe.

When OutKick reported something inconvenient for the league, FOS wanted documentation, competing sources and context about OutKick's motives.

But FOS's own report says the CBA does not define the central term, then prints an anonymous claim that Freedom and White are ineligible without explaining how the WNBA reached that conclusion.

The story gives readers no indication the reporter asked the league to define "woman," identify the eligibility criteria it applied to Freedom and White or explain whether self-identification would ever be sufficient. And if he did ask those questions, the story should have told readers that the WNBA wouldn't answer them.

It did neither.

Instead, readers got the WNBA's conclusion and its "publicity stunt" label, not the reporting needed to support either one.

For weeks, the WNBA said there were no immediate eligibility matters to address. Then unnamed league sources told Front Office Sports that Freedom and White are ineligible.

That is an eligibility determination.

The league reportedly made it. It now needs to explain the rule behind it.

item.title: Trump administration touts ‘hard reset’ for American schools, vows to put parents ‘back in charge’
item.description: The president, who was joined by Education Secretary Linda McMahon, said his education agenda will expand school choice, boost support for families and give parents a greater say in their children’s education.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Monday marked the back-to-school season by promoting his administration’s school choice agenda and pledging to put parents "back in charge" of where and how their children are educated.

Speaking at a White House event alongside Education Secretary Linda McMahon, students, parents and educators, Trump said his administration is working to expand school choice while removing what he called "far left extremism" from classrooms.

"We're putting the parents back in charge," Trump said. "They're the ones that love our children. They're the ones that should be in charge."

Trump argued that despite how much the U.S. spends on education, student outcomes should be stronger and families need more schooling options.

NEW YORK JOINS FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE INITIATIVE DESPITE TRADITIONAL DEMOCRAT OPPOSITION

"We want every parent to have the power to send their child to a high-quality school that shares their values. It's so important," Trump said.

The president highlighted the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which beginning in 2027, will offer taxpayers a credit of up to $1,700 for eligible donations to scholarship-granting organizations.

Those organizations can provide scholarships for education-related expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring, school fees and classroom supplies. The funds can also benefit students attending public schools.

The White House said nearly 52 million students could be eligible for the Education Freedom Tax Credit.

DEMOCRATS AIM TO KILL SCHOOL CHOICE FROM WISCONSIN TO THE REST OF THE US

Trump also highlighted changes to 529 education savings plans that allow families to withdraw up to $20,000 annually for K-12 expenses, doubling the previous limit.

Several parents joined Trump at the event to describe how expanded school choice could help their families.

Caleb Griffith, a North Carolina father of five who said his family includes two children with special needs, said the Education Freedom Tax Credit will give his children "access to the services they need to be successful in the most formative years of their lives."

"I want to tell you, we only get one chance to educate our children, and our children are the future of America," Griffith said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT

McMahon said the administration is seeking what she described as a "hard reset" in American education, with a goal of returning "to common sense."

"This school year, American parents and students have so much to be excited about because the Trump administration is steering education back to its rightful focus, serving students so that they are prepared for successful futures," McMahon said.

item.title: Mariska Hargitay nearly left 'Law & Order SVU' over fear of being a 'one-trick pony'
item.description: Mariska Hargitay revealed she once told Julianna Margulies she needed to leave "SVU," but her blunt response changed everything.
item.content:encoded:
Mariska Hargitay once considered leaving "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" after more than two decades as Olivia Benson because she worried the role had come to define her career.

In a new interview with Variety, the actress — who has starred as Benson since "SVU" premiered in 1999 — said she began questioning her future on the long-running NBC drama around its 25th season.

"I’ve got to leave the show too. I don’t want people to think I’m a one-trick pony," Hargitay recalled telling "ER" co-star Julianna Margulies.

'THE BIG BANG THEORY' STAR JIM PARSONS SAYS HE PAID A STEEP PRICE FOR FAME

Margulies, who famously left "ER" after six seasons, had a blunt response.

"Sweetheart, that ship’s sailed," Hargitay said Margulies told her.

While Benson made her a household name, the Emmy winner admitted she often felt constrained creatively due to the grueling production schedule.

"The comedy thing was painful to me because I felt like I was only exercising one part of myself," Hargitay said. "People would say, ‘You need to get off that show and do comedy. You need to get off that show and have a talk show.’"

‘X-FILES’ STAR GILLIAN ANDERSON REVEALS PARENTING REGRET, SAYS SHE WISHES SHE WAS 'LESS SELFISH'

"I wasn’t ready to leave, because I loved it," she said. "And then I got to do all this other stuff, and that’s why I don’t think about leaving right now. Do I want to quit now? No. Why? I made a movie while shooting; I did a play for six weeks on hiatus. I’m hosting the Emmys."

In 2023, Hargitay opened up to Fox News Digital about franchise creator and producer Dick Wolf's "great writing." 

"Dick Wolf is truly a visionary," she said Tuesday. "And I think that's a very singular thing to be a true visionary who understands our culture in a very deep way, but also understands it's sort of ironic that a crime show would be actually calming in a way to our nervous system, knowing that somebody is out there taking care of it."

She continued, "That our voices are heard and there are people that are on it. So that is it."

MARISKA HARGITAY JOKES ABOUT BEING LONGTIME ‘LAW & ORDER’ CO-STAR CHRIS MELONI'S ‘SECOND WIFE’

"It's a very sort of interesting dichotomy," Hargitay added. "Because you think about a crime show, which normally should sort of upset your nervous system, actually can settle it down because of that."

"Law & Order's" success spawned seven spinoffs, including "Special Victims Unit," "Criminal Intent," "Trial by Jury," "LA," "UK," "True Crime" and "Organized Crime."

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS SURPRISING REASON 'FRASIER' ALMOST NEVER HAPPENED

In 2019, "SVU" became the longest-running live-action television series in history. Hargitay has starred as Detective Olivia Benson in the police procedural since its premiere in 1999 and became an executive producer in 2016.

Fox News Digital's Larry Fink contributed to this post.

item.title: Oklahoma-based Southwest Airlines flight attendant found dead in Hawaii, police investigating
item.description: Oklahoma Southwest Airlines flight attendant Jenny Lupton's family fears foul play after she fell from the 24th floor of the Hilton Hawaiian Village.
item.content:encoded:
An Oklahoma-based Southwest Airlines flight attendant was found dead outside her hotel in Hawaii.

A spokesperson for the Honolulu Police Department told Fox News Digital that an unattended death investigation was launched for 50-year-old Jenny Lupton, whose family says fell off the 24th floor of her hotel in Honolulu, Hawaii.

According to News9, Lupton's family was told by the Honolulu Department of the Medical Examiner that she fell from her balcony off the 24th floor, as she was staying at the Hilton Hawaiian Village in Waikiki.

AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANT KILLED IN TOURIST HOT SPOT AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE SUSPECTED BOAT STRIKE

Tresa Lupton, Jenny's sister, said the flight attendant went out with her co-workers.

CARNIVAL CRUISE SHIP PASSENGER DIES AFTER FALLING FROM BALCONY – FBI INVESTIGATES HIGH-SEAS HORROR

"She just went out with one of her flight attendant friends, and they danced and had a good time," said Tresa Lupton. "She had gotten a tattoo while she was there."

Tresa Lupton said her sister was in Hawaii due to work and planned to stay for a few days before returning to Oklahoma.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

According to Lupton's family, hotel security told them that police are reviewing over 70 cameras that were in the area. Police aren't sure if anyone witnessed the fall.

Tresa Lupton said she's traveling to Hawaii to search for her sister, saying "the timeline doesn’t make sense, and we are afraid that maybe there was foul play."

The Honolulu Police Department said it won't be releasing more information until its investigation is complete.

item.title: Manhunt for Massachusetts woman ends with grim discovery week after police officer husband found dead at home
item.description: Police said preliminary evidence suggests Karen Solomon died by suicide after her body was found near a Worcester rehabilitation hospital, ending a dayslong search following her husband’s death.
item.content:encoded:
The body of a woman believed to be Karen Solomon, the missing wife of a veteran Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer found dead last week, was discovered in city woods Monday with a handgun nearby, authorities said.

Worcester Police Chief Paul Saucier said two Fairlawn Rehabilitation Hospital employees discovered the body while walking near the facility at about 12:40 p.m.

"Upon further examination, we believe this person to be Karen Solomon," Saucier said at a news conference, stressing that the identification is preliminary and still must be confirmed by the medical examiner.

Police said they believe Solomon died by suicide, Saucier said, adding that preliminary evidence showed she had a gunshot wound. Investigators recovered a handgun near her body, but Saucier said it was not a service weapon.

SPECIAL FORCES VET ACCUSED OF TRYING TO KILL WIFE FOUND DEAD, ENDING MASSIVE TENNESSEE MANHUNT

The department now believes the case was a "tragic murder-suicide," though the investigation remains ongoing, Saucier said.

Karen Solomon, 58, had been missing since her husband, Worcester Police Officer Kurt Solomon, was found dead inside the couple’s Wildwood Avenue home on Aug. 18.

Police responded to the residence at about 5:28 a.m. after receiving a report of a person down and found the off-duty Worcester police officer dead inside, authorities said. His cause and manner of death have not been released.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND

Authorities initially said Karen Solomon was a suspect they wanted to question about what happened at the home and warned that she was believed to be armed and dangerous.

The woman’s body was found about 0.6 miles from an area where police had released video showing Solomon walking behind an animal clinic, Saucier said. The Coes Pond area and park, which police had been searching since the first day of the investigation, spans about 90 acres.

Saucier said investigators cannot yet say when Solomon died. Police did not receive any reports of a gunshot being heard Monday, he said.

The chief also pushed back on speculation surrounding domestic violence. The case was described as domestic under Massachusetts law because it involved family or household members, he said, but added that the Solomon family had no history of domestic abuse.

The Solomon family said the "nightmare of the past week" had left them "heartbroken and rudderless" in a statement read by Saucier.

"The compassion, dedication and empathy of all the agencies involved have given us light in face of darkness," the family said, thanking local, state and federal law enforcement agencies that joined the search. "You have given us comfort knowing that you were working on our behalf for us."

SUSPECTS IN DEADLY CONNECTICUT HOME INVASION ARRESTED IN ATTACK THAT ROCKED BEACH TOWN

Police have disclosed few details about what happened inside the residence, citing the ongoing investigation.

Public records reviewed by The Associated Press show Kurt and Karen Solomon co-owned the Wildwood Avenue residence. Kurt Solomon also identified Karen Solomon as his wife in a 2016 bankruptcy filing, according to the AP.

The New England Police Benevolent Association identified Kurt Solomon as a 31-year veteran of the Worcester Police Department and remembered him as an "incredibly dependable officer, colleague and friend."

"Thirty-one years of service represents an extraordinary commitment to a community and to the profession of law enforcement," the association said. "Officer Kurt Solomon answered that call for more than three decades, and his service, friendship and dedication will not be forgotten."

The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Trump inauguration pastor says Dearborn Christians 'afraid' to speak out in Muslim-majority city
item.description: Lorenzo Sewell says Christians in Dearborn, Michigan, privately told him they are afraid to express their faith, accusing city officials of upholding Sharia law.
item.content:encoded:
A Detroit pastor who delivered a prayer at President Donald Trump’s inauguration says Christians in Muslim-majority Dearborn, Michigan, have privately told him they are afraid to publicly express their faith, while accusing local officials of giving Muslim residents preferential treatment under a "two-tiered justice system."

"Right now, the city officials in Dearborn specifically, they are giving Muslims preferential treatment," Lorenzo Sewell, senior pastor of 180 Church in Detroit, told Fox News Digital in an interview Monday.

"Now, how do I know that?" Sewell asked. "This is how I know that. Being a Black man in the city of Detroit, we go to Dearborn. We know that the police know how to enact justice in Dearborn. They know how to pull you over. They know that if they catch you shoplifting, we've had Black women that tried to elude the police and lost their lives in the city of Dearborn."

GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS

"So, as a Black man that has grown up around Arabs my entire life, I know that the Dearborn police can enact justice," he continued. "So, when someone is being assaulted and nothing happens, when someone's being assaulted and the police choose to look the other way, you can see clearly a two-tiered justice system." 

"So, the city council, instead of them renouncing Sharia law, they are actually upholding Sharia law," Sewell added.

Sewell recently went viral following remarks he gave at a Dearborn town hall where he said, "America, we have lost this city. This is a city that is no longer up under American laws; we are up under Sharia law. We will not have it anymore."

FORT WORTH PRINCIPAL PICK FACES BACKLASH, INVESTIGATION OVER SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS DEFENDING SHARIA LAW

CBS News reported last Wednesday that Dearborn police said they made 22 arrests following the "Christian Crusader March," led by conservative activist Jake Lang. Sewell attended the march, which took place near a regularly scheduled Dearborn City Council meeting where he later delivered his viral remarks.

In a statement, Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin said, "Our officers met a challenging and rapidly evolving situation with the professionalism this community expects, keeping everyone safe, protecting the constitutional rights of those who came to be heard, and allowing the City Council to complete its business. I could not be prouder of them."

DOJ WEIGHS CIVIL RIGHTS PROBE INTO FORT WORTH POLICE OVER ALLEGED FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATIONS

Sewell told Fox News Digital he is concerned about the growing presence of what he called Sharia law practices in the community.

"One of the examples that I see of Sharia law happening right here in the metro Detroit … in the city of Hamtramck, you are allowed right now to sacrifice animals, literally," Sewell said. "Number two, halal meat. If you go to a public school, you are literally eating meat that's sacrificed to idols, because, according to Sharia law, that's what — that's a lawful meat." 

"And I believe the most concerning to me is the call to prayer," he added. "There is no other place in the world that you can go and tell that country, although you are a majority Christian country, you can't go anywhere else in the nation and tell that country they have to change the way they express their religious beliefs."

CALIFORNIA LAWMAKERS' PUSH TO MAKE MUSLIM HOLY DAYS STATE HOLIDAYS SPARKS DEBATE OVER SCHOOL NEUTRALITY

In January 2023, the Hamtramck City Council voted to allow animal sacrifice, and the website for Dearborn Public Schools says, "Dearborn Public Schools ensures all meats served in our schools are certified Halal."

The certificate for the halal meat, partially in Arabic, reads in part, "We certify that the food processing facility of Saad Wholesale, Inc. in Detroit, MI, USA has been inspected and approved by our Islamic organization for processing, packing, and labeling of Halal Meat & Poultry Products by applying our procedures according to the Islamic Rites."

"I see the city council upholding Sharia law through things like the call to prayer, through things like halal meat, through having more Arab writing than they do actually English, by having the chief of police talk more about protecting the rules of Islam and Islamic leaders instead of protecting the rights of all Americans," Sewell continued.

"So you can see clearly when someone speaks freely, they can be attacked, and it'd be justified," he added. "I can give you a clear example. My wife had her life threatened. We had the guy's number, we had his address, we had everything, and the lieutenant did absolutely nothing. So, that's how you can see a two-tier justice system."

DEI HIRING BOOST FOR ONE BLUE STATE'S MUSLIM COMMISSION INITIATIVE FLIES IN FACE OF TRUMP'S ANTI-WOKE PUSH

He also claimed that Christians in the area feel afraid to express their faith.

"Since I went viral, I've had Dearborn Christians come out from the north, south, east, and west, and they're afraid," Sewell said. "I want you to think about this for a moment, America. Think about being in a Christian nation, being afraid to talk about Christ. I want you to just think about that for a moment."

"I'm having people say, 'I'm with you, but I'm afraid to say it,'" he continued. "'I'm with you, but I'm afraid to be by you.' 'I'm with you —' This is how we know we are in a two-tiered system because, in a Christian nation, we're afraid to be Christians."

TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS

Dearborn city council president Mike Sareini told Fox News Digital that the pastor’s claims are false.

"The City of Dearborn is an American city governed by the U.S. Constitution, the laws of the State of Michigan, and the City of Dearborn Charter," Sareini said. "Those laws apply equally to every resident, regardless of religion or background. Everyone is treated the same."

"There is no evidence of preferential treatment for any religious group. These accusations are unfounded, and I challenge anyone to present evidence otherwise," Sareini continued.

"Dearborn is home to approximately 30 churches and 10 mosques," he added. "Most recently, pastors from throughout Dearborn spoke at a press conference and publicly confirmed that people of different faiths live together peacefully in Dearborn, without the conflict being alleged."

Fox News Digital reached out to Dearborn mayor Abdullah Hammoud and the Dearborn Police Department for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: With one month left, American League teams are heading towards an embarrassing, historic low
item.description: The American League standings in 2026 could produce historic embarrassment as no AL West team holds a winning record with just a month remaining.
item.content:encoded:
There's a widespread assumption that parity is the greatest achievement any sports league can have. Nobody wants to see elite teams dominate, year in and year out, the thinking goes.

This appreciation for parity is frequently referenced as one of the explanations for the NFL's total and complete ratings domination. Though this parity is curiously never impacted by the fact that Patrick Mahomes or Tom Brady has won the Super Bowl in seven of the last 12 years, despite Brady having retired three years ago.

Still, if parity is what fans want, boy should they love the American League standings in 2026.

DESPITE COMPLAINTS ABOUT OTHER SPORTS, THE NFL HAS BECOME THE MOST PREDICTABLE LEAGUE IN AMERICA

We're barreling toward September and the end of the 2026 regular season, with most teams having just 30–32 games remaining on their schedules. And this year's AL, particularly the AL West, is on track to make a historic, embarrassing, type of history.

Since the founding of Major League Baseball, there's never been a team in a full season to reach the postseason with a losing record. Yet with, again, just over a month's worth of games remaining, there are only four teams in the AL with a winning record. Three of them are in the same division. It gets worse.

A LAUGHABLY BAD AMERICAN LEAGUE HAS ALLOWED ONE OF BASEBALL'S WORST TEAMS TO CLIMB INTO THE PLAYOFF RACE

Not one team in the American League West has a winning record, with the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers both tied at 65-66. The Seattle Mariners, who both bought and sold at the trade deadline, are in third place at 62-69. They've been outscored by 61 runs this year. Seven games under .500. Surely eliminated from postseason contention, right?

Not exactly. Somehow, the Mariners are just three games back of both first place in their division and the third wild card spot. Then there's the rest of the AL.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

The Cleveland Guardians are 65-66, and currently in the third wild card spot, tied with the Rangers. The Toronto Blue Jays, having a disappointing season after coming within two outs of winning the World Series in 2025, are just 1.5 games back despite a 64-68 record.

Then there's the Detroit Tigers, who gave up on their season and traded Tarik Skubal to the Dodgers, are only 3.5 games back, despite a 61-69 record. Impressively, even the 58-74 Kansas City Royals are "only" 7.5 games out of a wild card spot after winning eight in a row.

SMALL MARKET MLB TEAMS ARE OUTPERFORMING BIG PAYROLLS, UNDERMINING OWNERS' PUSH TO CANCEL 2027 SEASON

Running away with the best record in the AL is poor, downtrodden, small market Tampa Bay Rays, at 77-53, but between the fourth best record, the low payroll Chicago White Sox at 68-62, and the Tigers in 12th, the winning percentage gap is just five percentage points. Nine teams in the AL are projected to finish with between 77-83 wins. You want parity? Boy has baseball delivered parity.

11 teams in the AL have at least a 12% chance of reaching the playoffs, per Fangraphs. The Mariners have a 35% chance of reaching the playoffs with their current record sitting at 62-69. Hilariously, again, per Fangraphs, the Astros have a 16% chance of clinching a first-round bye with a losing record. Oh, and they just mutually agreed to part ways with their general manager, Dana Brown, because the team has been so underwhelming this year.

MLBPA OPENS CBA NEGOTIATIONS WITH PLAN TO PUNISH LOW-SPENDING TEAMS AND RAISE LUXURY-TAX THRESHOLD TO $300M

Meanwhile, in the National League, 10 of the 15 teams have a positive run differential, with the St. Louis Cardinals just behind at -2.

So why has this happened? Partially, it's a result of AL teams and owners putting profits ahead of building the best possible roster. Mid to small market teams in the NL have been more committed to higher salaries and more talent, like the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Diego Padres. Even when organizations, like the Blue Jays, have committed to trying to win, disappointing seasons from star players like Vladimir Guerrero Jr. have led to underwhelming records.

All these elements have combined to create a scenario where we could go from not a single team making the playoffs with a losing record in a full season, to multiple teams making it in the same season. Wild. And embarrassing.

But that all highlights the underlying truth about modern baseball: the gaps between teams just aren't that big. Yes, the Dodgers have vacuumed up talent. They also just went 2-11 against the Red Sox, Cubs, and Brewers. Advancements in pitch design, creation, and data has compressed the gulf between the best pitchers in baseball and the middle class.

Teaching starters to go max effort on every pitch, combined with the ease of finding fireballing relievers, has made run prevention easier to come by. Those factors have created this remarkable level of parity. Funny timing as the league and its owners look to lock players out in a few months over concerns about "competitive balance.

item.title: Schiff attack on Trump’s DC IndyCar race backfires after driver points out contradiction
item.description: IndyCar driver Graham Rahal fired back at Adam Schiff's claim that Trump's Washington race wasted taxpayer money, noting Penske privately funded it.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Adam Schiff’s latest attack on President Donald Trump was challenged by an IndyCar veteran who pushed back on the California Democrat's charge that the commander-in-chief was wasting taxpayer funds for his own "self-aggrandizing."

Schiff criticized Trump for ordering the Washington race by executive order and accused the president of using the motorsports "spectacle" to distract Americans from higher costs and policy failures.

"While you struggle with the cost of gas, Trump offers you the spectacle of an IndyCar race hoping you will not notice," Schiff said Sunday.

START YOUR ENGINES: HERE IS YOUR CRASH COURSE ON THE INDYCAR FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX WEEKEND

"More taxpayer money spent on his self-aggrandizing distractions. And you get higher taxes and higher costs," he added, although major automotive firm Penske said it bankrolled the event.

Schiff posted the criticism on X alongside video of Trump waving the green flag as FOX Sports announcer Leigh Diffey got the race underway.

PRESIDENT TRUMP REPORTEDLY WILL GO ON A LAP OF HONOR AROUND THE FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX STREET CIRCUIT

Race fans and other critics lambasted Schiff’s comments, including IndyCar driver Graham Rahal, who reminded the California Democrat that the race was privately funded and argued it benefited government coffers because thousands of spectators traveled to Washington and spent money.

"No, no, Adam. He wanted you to notice and bask in the pride of being American, watch great racing and patriotism on display," Rahal responded on X.

DRIVERS JOSEF NEWGARDEN AND KYLE KIRKWOOD TALK INDYCAR'S 'ONCE-IN-A-LIFETIME' FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX

"Not only that, this was privately funded, not government although it drove thousands of folks to the DC area that have never been. That’s economic impact for you," said Rahal, who finished 13th in the event. His father, Bobby Rahal, is a well-known motorsports driver and executive.

Rahal also argued that the event brought visitors to Washington who might not otherwise have seen the nation’s capital.

WORLD CUP ENERGY CARRIES INTO FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX AS GLOBAL FANS CELEBRATE AMERICA'S HISTORIC BIRTHDAY

"And guess what, hundreds of thousands of Americans, blue & red, as well as fans from all over the world loved the Freedom250."

"What kind of loser posts this?" added Breitbart editor Joel Pollak. "People had fun."

KYLE KIRKWOOD HANGS ON TO WIN FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX IN WASHINGTON

As Rahal noted, Penske Corporation picked up most of the race tab. The automotive and logistics company, based in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, and Reading, Pennsylvania, is led by Roger Penske, who also owns the Team Penske racing organization with drivers in NASCAR and IndyCar.

When Washington’s NBC affiliate interviewed Penske President Bud Denker at the track and asked who was paying for the Freedom250, Denker responded: "We are."

TRUMP SHOWCASES RAW AMERICAN MUSCLE IN PREVIEW OF FIRST-OF-ITS KIND AMERICA 250 GRAND PRIX

"When I say vast, the only part we're not paying is, we're raising some revenue by having sponsors with the suites I'm building [along the course]," Denker told the outlet, adding it was not intended to be a "break-even" venture.

Penske did not cover every expense. Security was handled by local and federal law enforcement, including through federal funding provided to Washington for major events, according to the NBC station.

RACER STING RAY ROBB GEARS UP FOR FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX: 'THIS IS MORE THAN JUST AN INDYCAR EVENT'

The White House also fired back at Schiff, saying the Democrat put his personal animus ahead of the American people.

"It’s a complete disgrace that Pencil-Neck Adam Schiff is willing to trash the United States of America during its historic 250th birthday celebrations simply because he hates President Trump," said White House spokesman Davis Ingle.

"The great people of California deserve better," Ingle said.

Former electronics executive Sam Antar also responded to the senator, saying the lawmaker "apparently didn’t bother checking who actually paid for the race before blaming Trump for ‘more taxpayer money spent’."

"Schiff saw Trump, started typing, and skipped the part where you check the facts first. That’s how you end up volunteering for your own Community Note," Antar said.

Conservative commentator "Bad Hombre" replied by posting an image of then-President Joe Biden posing with attendees at a White House lawn gala featuring transgender and LGBT activists.

"The race was privately funded by Penske/IndyCar, pencil neck," Hombre said.

"But now that we’re on the topic of taxpayer-funded events, why were you cool with forcing taxpayers to spend $1.3 million on this?"

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Trump has shown support for American motorsports, praising his friendship with Penske, becoming the first president since Ronald Reagan to attend a Daytona 500 and hosting several NASCAR drivers and the circuit's former CEO, Brian France, at campaign rallies.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rahal and Schiff for further comment.

item.title: Vance's decade-old ‘great regrets’ resurfaces as El-Sayed’s jab at second lady comes back to bite him
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's swipe at Usha Vance backfired after critics pointed to a passage in JD Vance's "Hillbilly Elegy" that directly undercut his attack.
item.content:encoded:
A decade before Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed appeared to question how JD Vance’s grandfather would have regarded Usha Vance, the vice president wrote that one of his "great regrets" was that his grandparents never got to meet his wife.

"Last, but certainly not least, is my darling wife, Usha," Vance wrote in 2016 in the acknowledgments of his memoir "Hillbilly Elegy." He added, "… though it is one of the great regrets of my life that Mamaw and Papaw never met her, it is the source of my greatest joy that I did."

The passage was cited repeatedly on social media over the weekend as conservatives dragged the Michigan Senate candidate over his swipe at second lady Usha Vance. The controversy comes as El-Sayed fights for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat against Republican Mike Rogers, putting the Democrat’s rhetoric under a brighter spotlight as the high-stakes general election takes shape.

VANCE UNLOADS ON EL-SAYED OVER SHARIA REMARKS: ‘THAT’S NOT MY GRANDPA’S DEMOCRATIC PARTY’

El-Sayed invoked Vance’s family after the vice president criticized his past comments about Sharia law at an Ohio rally this month, arguing that the Michigan Democrat represented a version of the party his grandfather — whom Vance called "Papaw" — would not have recognized.

"So do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no…" El-Sayed said, a remark critics called racist and interpreted as an insinuation that Papaw would not have accepted Usha because of her Indian heritage.

Critics were quick to call out El-Sayed, with many questioning his attitude toward women and others pointing to Vance’s book.

"Why does Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed just assume that all White midwestern grandparents are racist?" asked Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas.

EL-SAYED UNDER FIRE ONLINE AFTER TAKING AIM AT USHA VANCE, FEMALE TRUMP AIDE IN WEEKEND SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS

"El-Sayed is an absolute vile, abhorrent, PIG. Usha Vance is a beloved figure in our country and in my opinion Vice President Vance's most powerful secret weapon," said Meghan McCain. "Women in America truly love her – attack her at your own peril democrat psychopaths. It will backfire."

"If you’re a rural White American living in Michigan, just remember El-Sayed believes you’re a racist," said commentator Ryan Girdusky.

"You are a racist creep," said journalist Emily Schrader in response to El-Sayed's post.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed and the Vance family for comment.

"Hillbilly Elegy," published in 2016, chronicled Vance’s upbringing in Middletown, Ohio, and his family’s Appalachian roots in Kentucky, with his grandparents — whom he called "Mamaw" and "Papaw" — playing central roles in the memoir and his childhood.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

item.title: Shaquille O'Neal goes feral hog hunting in East Texas darkness: 'I am the nightvision'
item.description: Video shows Shaquille O'Neal firing into the darkness during a night hunt with Texas_NightHunter near Paris, Texas, declaring himself "the nightvision."
item.content:encoded:
It's a bad day to be a feral hog. At least when Shaquille O'Neal is around.

The 7-foot-1 NBA legend spent a night hunting hogs in East Texas last week with the crew behind Texas_NightHunter. And according to Shaq, he didn't need much help locating his target.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"I smell pigs," O'Neal says into the camera while standing in the darkness. "Some people need nightvision. I am the nightvision."

Moments later, Shaq fires his gun before eventually walking over to a hog on the ground and finishing it off.

CONTENT WARNING: The video below contains graphic footage of a hog being shot and killed.

For the record, we at OutKick OutDoors do not condone the no-look discharge of a firearm under any circumstances. Please do not do that.

The hunt took place near Paris, Texas, according to a Facebook post highlighting O'Neal's outing. He joined East Texas native Matthew Prescott and other members of the local crew, which has previously taken notable guests — including two-time Super Bowl champion Torrey Smith — out hunting.

And while Shaq stalking pigs in the dark makes for entertaining content, knocking down feral hogs in Texas is also doing landowners a favor.

A very, very big favor.

Texas has the largest feral hog population in the United States, with millions of the invasive animals roaming the state. Texas A&M AgriLife has reported that feral hogs cause more than $670 million in annual agricultural losses, while landowners spend an additional estimated $130 million or more each year trying to control them and repair the damage they leave behind.

The animals tear up crops, pastures, fences, roads and waterways, damage habitat used by native wildlife and can carry diseases capable of affecting livestock, wildlife and humans.

CODY JOHNSON FIRES BACK AT CRITICS, CALLS ALASKA GRIZZLY BEAR HUNT A 'CONSERVATIONIST EFFORT'

They're also notoriously difficult to control.

Feral hogs reproduce quickly, have few natural predators and have dramatically expanded their range. Texas A&M researchers have previously estimated that roughly two-thirds of a population would need to be removed annually for several consecutive years just to keep the numbers from growing.

So Texas isn't exactly worried about hunters like Shaq taking too many.

There are no closed seasons or bag limits for feral hogs on private property, and a hunting license is not required when hunters have landowner authorization. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department even specifically promotes nighttime hog hunting, noting that the animals become increasingly nocturnal during the hot summer months.

This also wasn't O'Neal's first rodeo — or "Shaqfari," as he calls it.

Hunting has been a longtime hobby for the four-time NBA champion. Over the years, O'Neal has hunted everything from waterfowl to wild boar and goats. He even devoted a section of his 2001 autobiography, "Shaq Talks Back," to his hunting adventures.

And if there were ever any question about whether a Hall of Fame big man belongs in the wilderness, O'Neal also tested that theory back in 2016 when he joined survivalist Bear Grylls for an episode of "Running Wild." Shaq trekked through the Adirondacks, climbed a massive rock face and spent the night sleeping outside in the woods.

So this wasn't some celebrity photo-op where Shaq showed up, held a rifle and went home.

The man just really loves a Shaqfari.

item.title: State Department blasts back at 'rogue judge' who overturned aggressive visa crackdown
item.description: The State Department blasted a "rogue judge" who vacated Marco Rubio's immigrant visa freeze on 75 countries as an exercise in Orwellian logic.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The State Department tore into the "rogue judge" who overturned its freeze on immigrant visas from 75 countries after she blasted the administration’s legal rationale as "an exercise in Orwellian logic."

"American taxpayer-funded public benefits belong to Americans," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told Fox News Digital. "President Trump has made clear that immigrants must be financially self-sufficient to protect these public benefits for American citizens."

"This rogue judge's misguided opinion wrongfully undermines the longstanding legal authority of the Secretary of State. We will keep fighting for commonsense visa policies that put America First."

U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas ruled Friday that the State Department could not force consular officers to deny immigrant visas to otherwise eligible applicants solely because they are nationals of one of the 75 countries covered by the policy.

BIDEN JUDGE OVERRULED ON KEY TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICY

Vargas, a Biden appointee who joined the Southern District of New York bench in November 2024, previously spent more than two decades as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan. She earned her undergraduate degree from Harvard University and a law degree from Yale, then clerked for future Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor on the Second Circuit.

Earlier this year, Vargas temporarily blocked Department of Government Efficiency personnel from accessing sensitive Treasury payment systems, citing privacy and cybersecurity concerns. But she later narrowed that order and allowed vetted and trained DOGE employees to access the systems.

Vargas found that Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s directive required officers to deny visas even after determining an applicant was not barred under any existing provision of immigration law. She vacated the policy and visa refusals based solely on the directive, sending those cases back for further consideration.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ORDERS GREEN CARD APPLICANTS TO LEAVE THE US, APPLY FROM THEIR HOME COUNTRIES

The Immigration and Nationality Act allows consular officers to deny immigrant visas to applicants they determine are likely to become a "public charge," meaning dependent on government assistance. Consular officers are supposed to make that assessment on an individual basis.

The Trump administration has revived a more expansive approach to that screening, directing officers to weigh factors including an applicant’s age, health, finances, English proficiency and potential need for long-term medical care.

TRUMP SCORES MAJOR IMMIGRATION VICTORY AS JUDGE CLEARS WAY TO END TPS PROTECTIONS FOR THOUSANDS OF SOMALIS

But Vargas found that the State Department went beyond that individualized review when it directed officers to refuse immigrant visas to otherwise eligible applicants from the 75 countries simply because of their nationality.

Fox News Digital first reported in January that the State Department would pause immigrant visa issuances to citizens of 75 countries, including Somalia, Afghanistan, Brazil, Nigeria, Russia and Iran, while it reassessed screening procedures meant to identify applicants likely to become a public charge.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The policy did not apply to tourist or other nonimmigrant visas. Affected applicants could still submit applications and attend interviews, but consular officers were directed to refuse immigrant visas under the pause.

The ruling does not require the State Department to issue visas to any particular applicant. Consular officers may still deny a visa based on an individualized public-charge finding or another statutory ground of inadmissibility.

item.title: Deshaun Watson says 'emotions got the best of me' after ripping Cleveland Browns fans for booing
item.description: Deshaun Watson addressed his "17 away games" comments after Browns fans booed him Saturday, offering an emotional explanation rather than an apology.
item.content:encoded:
It turns out Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson doesn't feel so great about the idea of playing "17 away games" after all, so he opened his press conference on Monday addressing his comments aimed at the team's fans and offered something of an apology.

Sort of.

Probably more an explanation.

DESHAUN WATSON FIRES BACK AT BROWNS FANS AFTER HE'S BOOED AT HOME

Whatever it was, once Watson was selected the team's starting quarterback on Monday morning, he got the message that ripping the fan base is not such a good idea – even if they booed him before, during and after he played in Saturday's preseason game.

"First off, I want to address the comments from Saturday after the game," Watson said to begin his presser. "I think just human nature and myself being very emotional, putting a lot of time these last two years to get back, spend time in this facility, in the city, meeting a lot of different people in the community, I thought I was going to get a little different response.

"But I think my emotions got the best of me, and my comments weren’t intended to go at any of the fans around the city, because there’s been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me."

Waiting for the apology.

"And I know the frustration. This organization put a lot of investment into getting me back in ’22, and things haven’t been going the right direction that we thought it would. A lot of injuries, a lot of time off, and not putting my best football and my best foot forward.

"So, again, I understand the frustration, I understand everything that goes into that."

BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QB DESPITE BOOING INCIDENT

Yeah, this an explanation. Not an apology for saying the fans had gotten "personal," and made him feel some sort of way about their reactions, which he deemed "disrespectful."

"I feel like I get more love on road games than I do at home games," Watson said at one point on Saturday. "So, if it is my [starting job] ... maybe it’s 17 away games, then."

To be clear: Browns fans have not embraced Watson for a number of reasons. He came to the team with a history of lawsuits tied to sexual abuse claims by nearly two dozen massage therapists in Houston.

He was suspended by the NFL 11 games and fined after he reached a settlement with those therapists as part of civil court proceedings.

Then Watson injured his shoulder in 2023, forcing him to miss 11 games. He tore his Achilles tendon in 2024, forcing him to miss 10 games. And he tore the same tendon again in 2025, forcing him to miss the entire season.

All this by a player who cost the Browns six draft picks in trade, including three first-rounders, and a fully guaranteed $230 million contract.

So, excuse the Dawg Pound if it took a big doodie on Watson by booing him on Saturday.

"Moving forward, I just want to focus on football, making sure that I’m putting the best product out there, having the best ability because I thrive off the energy," Watson said. "I thrive off the energy of the fans, I thrive off the energy of the community, I thrive off all that stuff.

"...I want to make sure I put the best product out there for the team, for the organization, and for the city, so we can put [out] a lot of wins, and celebrate, and put Cleveland on the map."

item.title: Sophie Cunningham throws on a backless top and overtakes Caitlin Clark, Trump waves the flag & Gruden's back!
item.description: Sophie Cunningham surpassed Caitlin Clark in WNBA social media followers, reaching 4 million as her popularity rockets toward the league's top spot.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Listen ... Just listen.

You hear it? You smell it? Really listen closely ...

It's officially college football week. We've made it. It's our first real game week since January. Really, it's our first one since December. I don't want to hear a single word about "It's only Week Zero!"

UNC WANTED THE DEION SANDERS EFFECT WITH BILL BELICHICK, ALONG WITH WINS. IT GOT SOMETHING MUCH DIFFERENT

Hogwash. Last I checked, we're getting a noon ESPN game featuring Bill Belichick on Saturday. That ain't Week 0. That's football.

We're back. We've made it. Last Saturday was our last Saturday without college football until 2027. Time to lock it in, boys and girls. Move over, WNBA, the real #content machine is back ...

... But first, welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham stuns in a backless halter top and then surpasses Caitlin Clark in social media followers.

What a day! Oh yeah. Something else happened in the WNBA last night. Honestly, I just don't feel like getting into it today. I'm tired. It's football season. I'm gonna sit this one out (sort of).

What else? I've got Trump angering the left by waving the green flag along the streets of D.C., Deshaun Watson somehow survived his asinine postgame presser to become the Browns' starter today (sorry, Cleveland fans), and Jon Gruden was BACK in the booth over the weekend.

And buddy, he was incredible. Here's an idea, CBS: Maybe pair him with Jim Nantz. Just a thought.

OK, let's get rolling. I've inexplicably got a fantasy football draft tonight even though it's Aug. 24. Unreal.

Grab you a waffle for National Waffle Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

Big day in the world of fast food, or whatever it is you consider Chick-fil-A. Is it fast food? It's a step above, for sure, but I don't know what I'd call it.

Anyway, they're rolling out their big Chicken & Waffles AND S'mores Milkshake today to coincide with National Waffle Day. Gives me a stomach ache just thinking about it, but I reckon it'll be good. Lord knows it'll be an absolute pleasure ordering it.

I maintain that there is no better food service business on the planet than Chick-fil-A. They are just incredible.

Anyway, let me know if you pop on over to one today and try it out. I don't see myself indulging any time soon given it's 110 degrees in Florida right now and Chicken & Waffles sounds just horrible, but I'm curious to hear your thoughts.

OK, now that the important stuff is out of the way, let's get this class started with Sophie Cunningham going with the backless top on social media before last night's game, and then surpassing Caitlin Clark in a big way when the dust settled:

That number says 4 million, folks. Why is that big? It now puts Sophie in second place in terms of follower count in all of the WNBA, ahead of Caitlin Clark.

Angel Reese is No. 1, for those wondering. She has over 5 million. Fair is fair, and I have to be fair to Angel here. The data says she's still No. 1. Kudos to her.

As for Sophie Cunningham, it's pretty clear she's a rocket ship right now in terms of popularity. The minority hates her, but don't be fooled, they are the minority. The data says she's a few months away from taking over the top spot in the WNBA. It's only a matter of time.

And when that happens, we can really start to laugh at people like this:

"The moment the league didn’t discipline Sophie Cunningham for her transphobic comments, they set the table for almost all of this political discourse and nastiness towards the trans community. Her conduct has objectively been detrimental to the league."

That's a real person, by the way. Chris Williamson is an "Emmy-nominated" sportscaster, per his X bio (which also features a picture of Angel Reese as the header).

Hilarious.

Again, let's quickly go back and see what those "transphobic" comments were in the original ESPN story:

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

That's it! Those are the transphobic comments! These people are the best. They're just the best. I can't get enough.

Speaking of delusional liberals, let's check in with Adam Schiff, who had a meltdown yesterday because Donald Trump waved the green flag for the IndyCar race in DC:

"While you struggle with the cost of gas, Trump offers you the spectacle of an IndyCar race hoping you will not notice," Shifty Schiff posted on Elon's X. "More taxpayer money spent on his self-aggrandizing distractions. And you get higher taxes and higher costs."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Hey, Shifty, cool it. Can we just enjoy some Freedom 250 racing action in peace, pal? It's a Sunday. We don't need to be serious every single day of the week. It's OK to give it a rest on a Sunday.

Looking at you, WNBA.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night of drafting an auction draft that I am 0% prepared for because it was sprung on me last night. Should end well!

First up? How about the NUTS on the Browns declaring Deshaun Watson QB1 after he took a blowtorch to the fanbase over the weekend?

That last one is the thing that really sticks out to me. Deshaun Watson isn't a good QB anymore. It's been YEARS since he was actually good at football. Years. And I was a huge Watson guy out of college.

But he's just genuinely bad at football now. Mix in just some ridiculous shots at a fanbase that has every single right in the world to despise him, and it's bonkers to me that they'd still name his the starter for Week 1.

Granted, Shedeur Sanders is no better at football, but at least he'd buy you a little grace with the fans.

I feel bad for old OutKick (and Nightcaps!) writer, Anthony Farris. I still talk to Anthony every day. He's hanging in there.

And by that, I mean he's miserable.

Next? You know who isn't miserable? Jon Gruden. How great was it to have Gruden back in the booth this weekend?

Nobody could break down a play better than Gruden back in the old MNF days. He was elite. One of one. Clearly, he still has the fastball. Lordy, I missed him.

Hey, CBS — I found your Romo replacement. Easiest call in the history of time.

You're welcome!

Now, let's go have a big week.

Is Week 0 the real start of the season? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Fox News' Emily Compagno joins 'The Five' as new co-host
item.description: Emily Compagno officially joins Greg Gutfeld, Dana Perino, and Jesse Watters as the new co-host of "The Five" starting September 8, Fox News announced.
item.content:encoded:

Compagno will make her official debut as a mainstay on "The Five" beginning Sept. 8. She will be joining longtime co-hosts Greg Gutfeld, Dana Perino and Jesse Watters as well as rotating hosts Harold Ford Jr. and Jessica Tarlov who fill the liberal seat at the table.

Emily is a highly accomplished host whose energy and talent have made her a standout across FOX News Media, and we are thrilled to officially welcome her to the show," Fox News CEO Suzanne Scott said in a statement.

FOX NEWS CHANNEL LEADS CBS AND NBC IN WEEKDAY PRIMETIME, DOMINATES CABLE VIEWERSHIP IN SECOND QUARTER RATINGS

item.description: Video shows tourists crowding within feet of a wild black bear at Mount Rainier National Park, ignoring the dangers of a close animal encounter.
item.content:encoded:
The willingness of people to walk up to animals in the wild will never cease to amaze. The lack of awareness of the dangers of doing so is astounding.

Last week, a crowd at Mount Rainier National Park tested their luck by getting insanely close to a wild black bear. For what, you might ask? For pictures and videos, of course.

The bear is doing bear things on the side of the path, you know, looking for something to eat, while tourists gather just a few feet away for the must-have shots of the wild animal in action.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Perhaps the only thing that is working in most of their favor is the fact that they only have to be faster than the slowest person in the group. That said, I wouldn’t recommend getting that close.

Who knows, what if the bear locks in on you, even though you're not the slowest one in the group? Sure, the footage would be incredible, but at what cost?

HIKER COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH MASSIVE BEAR ON POPULAR CALIFORNIA TRAIL IN TERRIFYING ENCOUNTER

Heading out to a national park and encountering wild animals isn't the same as going to the zoo. There's no enclosure slowing them down in the wild.

TOURISTS GET DANGEROUSLY CLOSE TO MASSIVE BISON IN STUNNING NATURE VIDEO POSTED ONLINE

One comment summed up the entire situation perfectly. The commenter wrote about the tourists crowding around the black bear:

"*David Attenborough voice-over* 'The Homo sapiens, each with the survival instincts of a ham sandwich, approach the juvenile bear who could rip their throat out in three seconds, and remark how cute he is. His mother is approaching from the south, and will soon demonstrate why bears will outlast humans as a species.'"

The bear isn't as cute as you think it is. These tourists are lucky they didn't personally have to find that out.

item.title: MLB broadcaster Alanna Rizzo on trans sports debate: 'I want to keep my stepdaughters safe'
item.description: Alanna Rizzo explains why she applauds Sophie Cunningham and wants to protect her stepdaughters' spaces from biological males in women's sports.
item.content:encoded:
Alanna Rizzo is one of the foremost authorities on Major League Baseball. This week, she joined OutKick for a wide-ranging discussion about the state of the sport, the Dodgers, a potential lockout and various pop culture topics.

Rizzo also has two stepdaughters. When asked about the ongoing debate over transgender athletes in female sports, she provided the perspective of someone with seemingly no interest in scoring points in the culture war.

"I believe everybody should have a right to be who they are, want to be who they are, be in a safe space, be protected, and feel that they can talk about things and have their own opinion on things," Rizzo told OutKick.

"But when it comes to physical space, especially for young girls and young women who may not have the resources, fortitude, or physical ability to protect themselves, I’m not saying that people are going in there and attacking them. But I grew up in sports my entire life.

"I would have been very uncomfortable with a male in my space. I ran cross country and track, so nothing to the level of Sophie Cunningham by any stretch of the imagination. I’m not a professional athlete by any scope of the imagination, but I would not have wanted a male in my space, nor do I want a biological male in the space of my young stepdaughters," she continued.

Rizzo disagrees that saying women should be protected in their own spaces is political, homophobic or transphobic.

"People think that if I say women should be protected in their own space, young girls, young women, women in general should be protected, that I’m anti-trans people or anti-gay. That’s not at all what I’m saying," she continued. "I think everybody should have the right to be who they are. But when it comes to physical space, I would not want a male in my space.

"I just don’t think that’s something that’s appropriate. And I just don’t see why it’s such a divisive issue. I think it should be common sense, but there’s nothing common about common sense, unfortunately."

FRANK ISOLA COMMENTS ON MICHAEL WILBON NAMING HIM PREFERRED 'PTI' CO-HOST WHEN TONY KORNHEISER RETIRES

Rizzo appreciated the awareness WNBA forward Sophie Cunningham brought to the topic.

"I, for one, applaud what Sophie Cunningham is doing. I think it's very difficult to speak your mind when everyone around you is against that thought process and against what you believe in. I do believe that there should be a safe space for everyone in this world, but I also believe in protecting young girls and young women. I want to protect my stepdaughters' spaces."

You can watch part of the segment below:

Notice what Alanna Rizzo says. She wants every person to have a safe space to play sports at every level. But to provide that, we cannot force females to compete against or change alongside males.

In addition to wanting to protect young girls, Rizzo has a foundation with the priority of protecting dogs.

"There's a lot of abandonment and neglect and surrendering of animals, and the overpopulation crisis is absolutely an epidemic, and a massive, massive problem. People are doing backyard breeding, unethical breeding, abandoning their pets, surrendering their pets at alarming rates and they're getting euthanized at alarming rates all across our nation, in shelters just because of space."

item.title: Clarence Thomas scorches racial litmus tests policing thought: ‘Stay Black and die’
item.description: Clarence Thomas compared restrictions on Black conservatives' viewpoints to racial segregation in a wide-ranging interview with Sen. Ted Cruz.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas rejected the idea that Black Americans should be expected to hold particular political views because of their race during a rare interview with Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz.

"We had this saying [that there are] only two things I have to do: stay Black and die," Thomas told Cruz, responding to a comment about the conservative justice having an individualist streak. "That was a retort to people who had these sort of requirements for us, these these mandates for us because of our skin color … But at any rate, they think that here's the way you're supposed to think. Again, here's your skin color. There's this kind of deterministic view that you're supposed to think this because we say so."

"And I, of course, declined that invitation. And so now that means that something, that I'm a walking contradiction because I've deviated from their perception of what I should think," the justice added while speaking on the "Verdict with Ted Cruz" podcast.

DEMOCRAT LAWMAKER CALLS CLARENCE THOMAS AN 'UNCLE TOM' AND 'LYNCHMAN' AFTER SUPREME COURT REDISTRICTING RULING

Thomas, who is Black, grew up poor in segregated Georgia, initially living in his parents’ wooden shack in Pin Point and later in Savannah with his grandparents. As a child, Thomas was raised speaking Gullah, a creole language derived from English spoken by the descendants of African slaves.

At the College of the Holy Cross, he initially embraced left-wing Black nationalism, admired Malcolm X and helped establish the school’s Black Student Union. Thomas began moving right after participating in a violent 1970 protest in Cambridge, Massachusetts, later saying his shame over the episode prompted him to reject left-wing activism and reconsider the self-reliance preached by his grandfather.

CLARENCE THOMAS WARNS AMERICA: LIBERTY DIES WHEN WE CHOOSE COMFORT OVER COURAGE

To further explain his point, Thomas compared efforts to dictate which ideas Black Americans should embrace to the restrictions of racial segregation.

"Here's what I've asked people. I said, ‘When I was a kid, the Savannah Public Library was segregated.’ I said, ‘Do you think it was right that the Savannah Public Library was segregated?’ Oh, no. You should have been able to go in," Thomas stated. "I said, ‘What if they allowed me in but said I couldn't go to certain floors? That would be wrong.’ I said, "What about if they said you couldn't go to certain stacks?’ Well, that would be wrong. ‘What if they had certain books marked that were off limits to me?’ That would be wrong."

BLACK GOP CONGRESSMAN SHUTS DOWN RACE QUESTION FOLLOWING SUPREME COURT REDISTRICTING RULING

"Then my question is, why is it then that you have a problem with me embracing certain ideas in certain books? What's the difference?’ Thomas went on.

item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin fires back at NFL returnee backlash: Blame the NCAA, not us for recruiting pro athletes
item.description: Lane Kiffin says LSU is recruiting athletes returning from NFL camps after court rulings granted NCAA eligibility the 2022 class was never told about.
item.content:encoded:
Lane Kiffin wasted no time Monday defending LSU’s decision to recruit players with NFL experience, or at least those who have recently participated in NFL camps.

Over the past few days, attention has centered around LSU deciding to go after some players who have recently been involved in NFL camps, thanks to a temporary restraining order granted by a judge in Louisiana.

While the focus has been on former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright, there are a number of other athletes that were given the opportunity for a return to college football.

NCAA Created This Mess, Now LSU Set To Make Dae’Quan Wright College Football’s First NFL Returnee

The reason why this has become such a hot-button topic is solely based on those players having already participated at the NFL level, besides playing in a regular season game.

NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME

But, thanks to the court ruling, the ability to come back to college for a fifth year is on the table for a number of players, with a few of them likely headed to Baton Rouge for a final season of college football.

If you expected Lane Kiffin to apologize for his involvement, you don't understand the LSU head coach.

On Monday, he opened his press conference by outlining the reasons why LSU was recruiting these athletes who were granted an additional year.

"So, you know, we have you know made a decision to recruit some kids around the country, and through these multiple injunctions around the country, which, this is not a first time in college sports, a group of players were granted a fifth year of eligibility, in multiple sports. And through them winning their injunction and entry into the portal, they’re available to recruit," Kiffin noted.

"So ourselves, like many places around the country, are recruiting them. At the end of the day, you know, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country. So, we made a decision to recruit them, like probably most people are."

One of the most interesting parts about this entire ordeal is the SEC's policy on players transferring within the conference, outside of the normal portal period. Since Dae'Quan Wright, and others, made a pit-stop in the NFL, the Tigers might have a different interpretation of the rules set forth by the SEC.

The question has obviously been a hot-button topic over the past few weeks, with a number of players going back to college after trying their hand at the NFL through either rookie mini camps or training camp.

How comfortable is Lane Kiffin with NFL players coming back to college? Well, every situation is different according to the LSU head coach.

FORMER FLORIDA STATE QB THOMAS CASTELLANOS SUING NCAA, SEEKS PORTAL ACCESS AFTER LANDMARK ELIGIBILITY RULING

"That's a good question," Kiffin noted. "I think that situations are different. In general, should NFL players come back to college? It's not necessarily what I believe, but that answer would be no. I think every circumstance should be looked at differently. This is a very unique circumstance, because I think there's not a lot of education on how this happened.

"The judge found that these players should have been told and should’ve known that they weren’t going to be eligible for a fifth year. Which, every athlete moving forward has. They should’ve known that in December when they were making decisions. Had they known that, they would have stayed...They did not know they had a year"

COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS

So, what changed? Well, multiple courts in different states have let it be known with their rulings that the NCAA was at-fault for not including the 2022 class in their new eligibility guidelines.

"Since then, a judge has said you do have a year," Kiffin continued. "Because of that, this is a different situation where they are wanting to go back to play the year they've been granted. This is a lot of athletes around the country, and a lot of these around the country that for my information isn’t stopping. There are cases right now where there are other athletes in the same cases.

TENNESSEE COACH UNLOADS ON NCAA'S 'BULLS–T', AFTER STAR LINEBACKER SUSPENDED FOR OUTDATED RULE

"So, you may end up having hundreds of athletes in this case that are told they have a fifth year. So, this is a really unique circumstance that isn’t traditional, just pros going back to college because they win a case."

I understand the LSU head coach can be an easy target.

But, nothing he said was wrong.

This falls on the NCAA deciding in June that they would install new guidelines around eligibility pertaining to athletes. And, in doing so left out the 2022 class all together.

So, while it might be easy to pile-on Lane Kiffin, which sometimes he does bring on himself, you can't fault one coach for doing something that another might not do in the same circumstance.

We've seen Dan Lanning and Marcus Freeman come out against adding players this late in the process. But, that is their decision.

Lane Kiffin, along with others, have decided that they will take advantage of where the NCAA screwed up to begin with, and judges are agreeing with those athletes.

Sure, we might not agree with NFL players coming back to college football. And, it's already started a war on social media. But, that doesn’t take away the fact that other schools are benefitting from these rulings, just as LSU is doing right now.

You can be mad all you want at the current situation, but don't forget who started this.

That would be the NCAA.

item.title: Terror threat looms over coastal destination as US warns attacks could strike without notice
item.description: Terrorists have targeted upscale lodges where international big-game hunters stay in Mozambique's Cabo Delgado Province, the State Department warns.
item.content:encoded:
Americans are being warned to avoid parts of an African safari destination where terrorists have targeted upscale lodges frequented by international big-game hunters.

Mozambique, a southeastern African country across from the island of Madagascar, is the subject of an Aug. 21 updated "Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution" advisory from the U.S. State Department.

Officials have also designated multiple areas "Level 4: Do Not Travel" — citing heightened terrorism risks.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

Bordered by Tanzania, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Eswatini, Mozambique is known for its Indian Ocean coastline, beaches and wildlife reserves.

Though not a tourist hot spot, Mozambique draws visitors for its safari tourism. It welcomed over 757,400 foreign guests in 2024, according to government statistics.

Cabo Delgado Province, a "Do Not Travel" area, is home to safari and wildlife destinations, including Quirimbas National Park.

The State Department also warns that terrorist groups in northern Mozambique are "active" and that there is a risk of terrorist violence and attacks.

ROBBERIES, ASSAULTS AND RAPES SPUR NEW US TRAVEL WARNING FOR POPULAR CARIBBEAN GETAWAY

"Attackers may strike public areas and tourist destinations with little or no warning, sometimes taking hostages," the advisory says.

Alex Perry, an England-based author and veteran foreign correspondent who previously served as a TIME bureau chief, told Fox News Digital the terrorist presence in northern Mozambique is relatively small but particularly brutal.

"Mozambique has one of the smaller ISIS groups in the world," Perry said, estimating it has roughly 500 members. "They are spectacularly nasty."

Perry, author of the book "Blood Will Flow" about the deadly Islamist insurgency in Mozambique, said militants in Cabo Delgado have carried out mass beheadings, and that the region's tourism industry has suffered as a result of the insurgency.

Cabo Delgado has historically attracted a more exclusive clientele, with smaller numbers of wealthy visitors paying high prices for hunting safaris compared with Africa's major mass-market safari destinations, he also said.

"This is almost exclusively hunting safaris — people going to shoot animals," Perry said. "That tends to be much smaller numbers of people paying a much higher price."

The State Department says Americans who opt to travel to Mozambique are encouraged to enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP).

Those who must travel to affected areas of Cabo Delgado, Niassa and Nampula provinces are also advised to consider hiring a security firm.

"Have evacuation plans that do not rely on U.S. government assistance. Have travel documents up to date and easily accessible."

Perry said that, although the advisory highlights serious risks, much of Mozambique remains a beautiful destination for travelers.

"On the whole, it's a pretty safe and secure and, as I say, beautiful and enjoyable place to visit," Perry said. "The far north is a dramatic exception."

The warning is one of several travel advisories issued or updated by the State Department in recent months, as officials continue flagging safety concerns for Americans traveling abroad.

item.title: El-Sayed distances himself from Hasan Piker after disturbing remarks about Jewish Americans

DEMOCRATS 'WHO NEVER VOTED REPUBLICAN' BACKING THIS GOP SENATE NOMINEE

After a combustible and divisive Democratic Senate primary in which El-Sayed narrowly edged more moderate Rep. Haley Stevens for the nomination, Rogers is heavily courting Democrats disaffected with their left-wing nominee.

But Lowenstein, who also sits on the Michigan Democratic Party Central Committee, said those behind the letter "are passionate about this and feel it’s an existential issue, and I think that represents a lot of people. And, so, they have to do what they have to do."
